Oral and maxillofacial surgery · published research

Jaw osteonecrosis (MRONJ/ORN)

Small nonrandomized reports describe symptom improvement or healing, but effects cannot be isolated from surgery, medication, or other laser approaches.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small nonrandomized reports describe symptom improvement or healing, but effects cannot be isolated from surgery, medication, or other laser approaches.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact MRONJ/ORN category contains 51 unique titles. It includes 24 primary nonrandomized patient reports, one review that also presents a case report, eight animal studies, five in-vitro records, 11 reviews or syntheses, and three guideline or other items. The database does not identify a human randomized trial in this exact category; a review of nonrandomized studies is not an RCT. (Vescovi et al. 2007 Vescovi et al. 2008)

Human and clinical evidence

Patient reports comprise case reports, case series, single-arm studies, retrospective cohorts, and one nonrandomized controlled study. Vescovi et al. described 19 patients treated with conventional care alone or in combination with Nd:YAG laser biostimulation. A later 28-case report described clinical improvement in some treated patients. These reports include different adjuncts and treatment pathways; overlap between publications cannot be ruled out. No randomized human evidence is indexed.

Animal evidence

Eight animal publications are listed (rat and mouse models), examining biological and tissue responses in osteonecrosis models.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Five in-vitro or ex-vivo studies are indexed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The records combine PBM, photodynamic therapy, and ablative or surgical laser procedures, with variable co-treatment by surgery, medication, or local care. Wavelengths, device settings, and schedules are not reported consistently enough to define a general PBM protocol. Findings from one laser type should not be attributed to all approaches.

Interpretation

Clinical reports are vulnerable to selection bias, publication bias, and confounding by surgery and medical co-interventions. Positive case outcomes warrant further study but do not establish causal benefit. Trials should define MRONJ and ORN separately, distinguish PBM from photodynamic or ablative approaches, and use controlled designs with standardized healing, pain, infection, and recurrence outcomes.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for human healing of MRONJ or ORN

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category contains 51 titles, but many are reviews, case reports, case series, or retrospective studies. The literature mixes PBM, photodynamic therapy, and ablative procedures, often with surgery or medication. No human randomized trial is identified in the source records. Controlled prospective studies are needed.
